learning_objective: 🎯 Discover how managers instruct, guide, inspire, and lead employees to put plans into action and achieve organisational goals!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Directing means instructing, guiding, counseling, and leading people. It initiates action, takes place at every level of management, and is a continuous process flowing from top to bottom.

Motivation stimulates people to action. Abraham Maslow identified 5 human needs: 1. Physiological (food/shelter) -> 2. Safety -> 3. Social/Belonging -> 4. Esteem (respect) -> 5. Self-actualization (achieving potential).
Financial incentives include pay, bonus, and profit-sharing. Non-financial incentives satisfy psychological needs, like employee recognition, job security, and career advancement.
1. Autocratic (boss takes all decisions), 2. Democratic (boss consults subordinates before deciding), 3. Laissez-faire/Free-rein (subordinates take their own decisions).

Communication is exchanging ideas. Barriers disrupt it: Semantic (language/jargon), Psychological (premature evaluation), Organisational (strict rules), and Personal (lack of confidence in subordinates).

fun_activity.title: 🎭 Style Switcher
fun_activity.instructions: Pick a scenario: 'Planning a surprise party'. Write one sentence on how you would lead the planning using an Autocratic style, one using Democratic, and one using Laissez-faire!

exam_tips: 📌 Planning, Organising, and Staffing are preparation for work. Directing is where the ACTUAL work (action) begins.
📌 Maslow's theory assumes that a satisfied need no longer motivates a person; they move to the next higher need.
📌 In case studies identifying communication barriers, look out for 'technical jargon' (Semantic barrier) or 'distrust' (Psychological barrier).
quick_recap: ⭐ The four elements of Directing are: Supervision, Motivation, Leadership, and Communication.
⭐ Grapevine is the informal communication network that spreads information rapidly (often rumors).
⭐ Effective leadership can turn an average team into a high-performing team.
